correctness.rationale: All-size induction classifies same-level versus new-level prime extensions, establishes the exact marked relative-rank factorization, derives the weighted split recurrence and recursively proves the canonical witness criterion. Every finite rank threshold has unique least size \(2^{t+1}-t-2\) by a forced induced embedding. The standalone checker independently enumerated all 2,047 positive host words through eleven vertices and 627,231 marked states and compared direct extension-game minimax to the theorem; 1,200 randomized additional profiles and the rank-six canonical sizes passed. These finite tests are corroborative, not a replacement for induction.

value.rationale: The problem is the structure of the new Fraïssé one-point-extension rank in a natural non-free-amalgamation class with two competing extension mechanisms: adding a tied element or inserting a new ordered class. The result is an exact all-size and all-marked-substructures theorem, identifies a single forbidden induced witness at every finite-rank threshold, proves unique minimal hosts and sharp exponential-minus-linear sizes, and offers a constructive decision test. These consequences are structurally informative and not an arbitrary parameter slice.
